speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To understand the cause of these symptoms, can you tell me if your weakness is getting worse over time or if it fluctuates throughout the day?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That pattern of worsening weakness with activity and improvement with rest, along with diplopia on vertical gaze, strongly suggests myasthenia gravis. To confirm this, do you have any known history of thymoma, or have you noticed droopy eyelids or difficulty swallowing?
